summary: The note describes the Tomb of Pope Julius II, a sculptural and architectural ensemble by Michelangelo and his assistants. It was commissioned in 1505, intended for St. Peter's Basilica, but completed in 1545 on a much reduced scale and placed in San Pietro in Vincoli in Rome instead. The church was linked to the della Rovere family, Julius's family, and Julius had served there as titular cardinal.
one_line: Michelangelo's tomb for Pope Julius II, commissioned in 1505, finished in 1545 at reduced scale, and placed in San Pietro in Vincoli, Rome.
key_facts: The Tomb of Pope Julius II is a sculptural and architectural ensemble by Michelangelo and his assistants.
The tomb was originally commissioned in 1505.
The tomb was not completed until 1545, and then on a much reduced scale.
The tomb was originally intended for St. Peter's Basilica.
After the pope's death, the tomb was instead placed in the church of San Pietro in Vincoli on the Esquiline in Rome.
The church of San Pietro in Vincoli was patronized by the della Rovere family.
Pope Julius II came from the della Rovere family.
Julius II had been titular cardinal of San Pietro in Vincoli.
